title: Phase 2: WORLD DATA - Complete Research with Web Sources
description: Weeks 5-8 - Playable world with states and geographic data. Research compiled from web sources with detailed implementation.

web_sources: Game Developer Deep Dive - Modeling Economy
Attack of the Fanboy - Goods guide

web_definition.what_is: States are the main political-geographical unit in Victoria 3 where pops live and buildings are built. They are based upon State Regions which are predefined parts of the map that can be subdivided into multiple split states.
web_definition.what_exists: Victoria 3 has 673 state regions globally, organized into 58 strategic regions. States inherit features from State Regions including State Traits, Arable Land, Resource Potential, and Hubs.
web_definition.how_to_use: Players interact with states for most economic actions. A State is controlled by a single country with dynamic borders that can change during gameplay. State Regions have static borders throughout the game.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: States can be Incorporated (fully integrated) or Unincorporated/Colonial. Incorporated states incur full taxation and consumption but cost bureaucracy. Unincorporated states have reduced taxes (-20%) and no consumption taxes.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Split states occur when multiple countries own provinces within a single State Region. Resources are divided proportionally based on province share.

key_details.state_vs_region: A State is always controlled by a single country and has dynamic borders. A State Region can contain one or several States and has static borders.
key_details.split_state: When two or more countries each own a portion of a State Region, they each control individual States within it. Resources are divided proportionally.
key_details.incorporation: Incorporated states are fully integrated political units. Unincorporated/Colonial states have reduced taxation (-20%) but lower bureaucracy cost.
key_details.hubs: Each state has up to 5 settlement types: City, Farm, Wood, Port, Mine. These appear visually based on related building levels.
key_details.traits: State Traits represent geographical features affecting economy. Examples: 'state_trait_bergslagen', 'state_trait_scandinavian_forests'.

capped_resources: resource type capped by state size

2_2_terrain_types.title: 2.2 Terrain Types - Combat and Movement Effects

web_definition.what_is: Terrain categories define the geographical nature of map tiles and affect combat, movement, and production.
web_definition.what_exists: Victoria 3 has multiple terrain features per province. Each feature adds to combat width calculation. Terrain provides modifiers to defense, offense, movement cost.
web_definition.how_to_use: Terrain affects combat width: combat_width = (5 + 0.5 × infrastructure) × terrain_multiplier. Mountain provinces increase combat width dramatically, reducing enemy advantages.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Terrain is set per province in map data. Each province can have multiple terrain features (e.g., mountain province has both 'elevated' and 'hazardous').
web_definition.how_to_expand: Custom terrain features can be defined and applied to provinces through map modding.

terrain_statistics_vic2.note: Victoria 3 uses similar system but modified

victoria_3_combat.terrain_modifiers: Each province has one or more terrain features. Weight is added for each feature present.
victoria_3_combat.combat_actions: Battles continue until one side runs out of morale or manpower. Winner advances front based on occupation value.

web_definition.what_is: Resources are materials that drive economic simulation, building construction, military production, and population welfare. They include both base resources and discoverable resources.
web_definition.what_exists: Victoria 3 has four main resource types: Staple (food, wood), Industrial (iron, coal, rubber, lead), Luxury (silk, tea), Military (small arms, ammunition). Discoverable: Oil, Gold, Rubber.
web_definition.how_to_use: Resources determine building capacity in states. Each state has Arable Land (agriculture limit) and Resource Potential (mining limit). Buildings produce goods consumed by pops and other buildings.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Resources are tied to State Regions. Arable land limits agriculture/plantation buildings. Resource potential limits mining/extractive buildings. Discoverable resources need technology to be discovered.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Resources can be discovered during gameplay through technology. Oil, gold, and rubber are discoverable. Discovery chances increase with certain technologies.

staple.description: Basic consumption goods for population needs

industrial.description: Resources used by buildings for production

oil.extraction: Oil Rigs (requires Pumpjacks technology) or Whaling Stations
oil.technology_unlocks: Pumpjacks after Steam Donkey and Dynamite

resource_limits.proportional_split: Split states divide resources by province share

web_definition.what_is: Country definitions define every playable or non-playable nation in the game world with attributes like government, culture, religion, and territory.
web_definition.what_exists: Victoria 3 has playable countries (selectable), AI-only nations, decentralized (tribal), and formable nations. Countries have tags, colors, cultures, religions.
web_definition.how_to_use: Players select a playable country at game start. Countries own states, have governments, cultures, religions, treasuries, prestige.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Country data includes: tag, name, color, government type, primary culture, religion, capital state, owned states, market membership.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Mods can add new countries, change historical data, create formable nations.

web_definition.what_is: Infrastructure determines how connected a state is to the market. Market access affects production efficiency and price volatility.
web_definition.what_exists: Infrastructure comes primarily from railways and ports. States require connection to market capital. Isolated states have 0% market access.
web_definition.how_to_use: Higher infrastructure = better market access = more efficient production. Overseas states require convoys for market access.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Market access = percentage based on infrastructure and connectivity. Low access reduces efficiency and causes price issues.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Build railways, ports, and other infrastructure. Maintain shipping lanes for overseas territories.

key_details.market_access_calculation: Primarily percentage based on infrastructure and connection to market capital
key_details.tax_capacity: 1 point per 10,000 population for full tax

web_definition.what_is: Systems for generating or loading map data including provinces, states, countries, and initial conditions.
web_definition.what_exists: Victoria 3 uses province map (provinces.png) + state region definitions. Map data in map_data/state_regions/. Can use GeoJSON, custom JSON, or heightmap formats.
web_definition.how_to_use: Load province IDs from map image (hex color codes). Define state regions with provinces, traits, hubs. Create states in history files.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Parser reads map format → converts to internal province/state/region structures → validates adjacency and completeness.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Procedural generation using noise functions. Hybrid: base terrain procedurally + handcrafted refinement.

definition.state_region: STATE_NAME = { id, provinces[], traits{}, city, farm, port, mine, wood, arable_land, resources }
